texts.preamble: In Re vs A-1) Manohar Singh on 28 October, 2016 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 65/01 Unique Case Id No. 02403R00170620 Date of Institution: 11.07.2001 Date of reserving judgement: 01.10.2016 Date of pronouncement: 28.10.2016 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A-1) Manohar Singh [Since Expired] A-2) Subhash Chand [Since Discharged] A-3) Vinod Kumar [Since Discharged] A-4) M/s Prabhu Dayal & Co. 458, Khari Baoli, Delhi-110006 ... Accused Persons Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules
texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules . The accused no.4 is a partnership firm from both premises food article, that is, Dal Chana, was lifted for sampling. Accused no. 1,2 and 3 are stated to be its partners, out of whom accused no. 1 was the vendor in whose presence the sample was taken. 2. As per the complaint, on 12.09.2000, food officials consisting of Food Inspectors (FI) Arun Kumar and Virender Singh under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. G.R.Meena reached along with their staff at the premises of accused no. 4 at 458, Khari Baoli, Delhi-110006 where accused no. 1 was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Dal Chana from the vendor lying in open gunny bag (ready for In Re vs A-1) Manohar Singh on 28 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139439220/ 1 sale) bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 25.09.2000, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it contained rodent excreta along with dead and living insects. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by the FI. It was found that accused no. 2 and 3 were also the partners of accused no. 4 firm in addition to accused no.1 vendor. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court by FI on 11.07.2001 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a),(b),(f),(h) and (l) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 11.07.2001. The matter was then listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh. Arun Kumar and PW-2 FI Virender Singh. 4. In the meanwhile, accused no. 1 expired and proceedings against him stood abated vide order dated 26.03.2009. On the basis of pre-charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused no.4 firm on 24.08.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a),(b) and (f) of PFA Act, to which it pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. At the same time, accused no. 2 and 3 were discharged by the court. 5. After framing the charge, the witnesses examined in pre-charge stage were recalled for further cross-examination in post charge stage. Additionally, the complainant examined PW-3 Sh. G.R.Meena in post charge stage. 6. PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 who were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings, deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 12.09.2000 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 750 grams of Dal Chana (ready for sale) lying in an open gunny bag, thoroughly mixing it using a clean and dry jhaba, dividing it into three parts by putting in three clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice as per Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. On the next working day, that is 13.09.2000, one counterpart of sample along with Memo as per Form-VII were sent to Public Analyst (PA) for analysis vide PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/D and remaining two counterparts with copy of Memos were deposited with LHA/SDM vide receipt Ex. PW- 1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received and upon direction of SDM/LHA, further investigation was carried out by PW-1. PW-1 issued letter to the accused in response to which he received reply Ex. PW-1/G alongwith documents Ex. PW-1/H and Ex. PW-1/J. They also received reply Ex. PW-1/K from the Sales Tax Department. Thereafter, sanction Ex. PW-1/L was taken from the Director PFA and after completion of the investigation, complaint Ex. In Re vs A-1) Manohar Singh on 28 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139439220/ 2 PW-1/M was filed in the court. After this, intimation letter Ex. PW-1/N with copy of PA report was sent to the accused persons through registered post vide postal receipt Ex. PW-1/O. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence counsel wherein they denied that the accused persons had been falsely implicated. They however accepted that no insect was noticed by them through naked eyes at the time of sampling. 7. Statement of the accused no.4 (through its AR) under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 05.05.2012 wherein it denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. It accepted the proceedings dated 12.09.2000, though claimed that no efforts were made to join public witnesses and no price of sample was paid to the vendor. It claimed that neither the firm nor its partners received the PA report. It took defence that the method of taking sample was not proper as it should have been taken by quartering system and preservative should have been added. It further claimed that its right under Section 13(2) PFA Act stood frustrated due to delay in filing the complaint. It further stated that the report does not specify the identity of insects, whether larva, pupa or fully grown insects. No defence evidence was however led by the accused no.4. 8. Record shows that accused no. 4 continued to appear in the court through its AR as well as Ld. Counsel but it was informed on 24.09.2013 that the said AR expired on 23.08.2013. Court notices were issued to the accused no.4 but there was no representation on its behalf. Subsequently, vide order dated 05.09.2016, the court directed to proceed against accused no. 4 firm ex-parte in view of Section 305 CrPC read with Section 17 of PFA Act because no person had been authorized by the said firm to represent it after the death of the previous AR and no coercive measures could be taken against such a fictitious entity. Therefore, no arguments have been advanced on behalf of accused no.4. 9.
texts.arguments: It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused no.4 firm beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that it has not been able to rebut the findings of the PA report dated 25.09.2000. It is pointed out that the accused no.4 has failed to exercise its right under section 13(2) PFA Act and failed to get the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. It is the defence of accused no. 4 that the PA report and intimation letter were never served upon it and it was prevented from exercising its right under section 13(2) PFA Act. It is further its defence that the nature / identity of the insects has not been given by the PA in the absence of which insect infestation cannot be established. It is also claimed that there has been a delay of ten months in filing the complaint which also frustrated the right of the accused no.4 under Section 13(2) PFA Act. 11. 13. Going by this provision, Section 17 lays down that in case of a company (which also includes a partnership firm), any person incharge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business can also be held liable in addition to the company. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Section 2(ia)(f) of PFA Act deals with situation where the article consists of any filthy, putrid, rotten, decomposed or diseased animal or vegetable substance or is insect infested or is otherwise unfit for human consumption. 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.

It is the defence of accused no. 4 that the PA report and intimation letter were never served upon it and it was prevented from exercising its right under section 13(2) PFA Act.
